newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Inchcape sells quality unit for cash.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Inchcape sells quality unit for cash.

text.p: Struggling British motors and distribution group Inchcape Plc arranged a needed injection of cash with Wednesday's disposal of its quality testing unit, but the move leaves it reliant on less profitable sectors.

In a statement that had been expected since the group announced in March plans to trim its structure this year, it said it had sold Inchcape Testing Services (ITS) for about 380 million pounds ($594 million).
The cash will be used to reduce most of the group's borrowings, which at the end of 1995 stood at a net level of 463 million pounds.
At the same time about 180 million pounds of exceptional pretax profit will be transfered to reserves.

"The sale is consistent with the new strategy we announced in March, and is a major step towards focusing Inchcape as an international distribution group," chairman Sir Colin Marshall said in a statement.

The plan is intended to leave the company better concentrated on its main activity of motor import and distribution along with marketing electronics and bottling soft drinks. It also calls for the divestment of another unit.
Wednesday's statement made no reference to its Bain Hogg insurance broking arm, which it has also decided to let go.
But the absence of any comment implies that the company still expects that a demerger is the most likely option, as managing director Philip Cushing said three weeks ago.
Marshall and Cushing have said repeatedly since March that both the planned divestments will be done by the end of 1996, which leaves them relatively little time to roll out a demerger.
Both Bain Hogg and Inchcape Testing are businesses that generate operating profit at a much richer rate per pound of turnover than either motor trading or marketing.

In the first half, for example, testing made an operating profit of 15.7 million pounds on sales of around 167 million. Analysts' expect it will make a final contribution to Inchcape's accounts of about 25 million pounds for 10 months of 1996.

Group operating profit from all the ongoing businesses, in contrast, was 72.4 million pounds on sales of 3.19 billion pounds in six months, while testing and Bain Hogg together made a total 36.5 million profit on their sales of 294 million.

However, despite the earnings dilution likely to stem from Wednesday's sale, Inchcape is convinced it can move forward with more confidence by selling the businesses and ploughing the proceeds into the foundations of its new future.

Share analysts believe that this strategy is still itself in a test phase, and since an initial burst of high hopes pushed up the stock price over 3.00 pounds in the first weeks of April it has lost momentum and fallen back, reflecting uncertainty.
After today's disposal news the shares rebounded modestly from their latest lows near 265 pence.
But the retracement to 275-1/2 pence, up 7-1/2 pence, by 1220 GMT, brought them only a little way back towards the level of 290 pence seen at the time of interim results last month. ($1=.6401 Pound)
